signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + JPY Outperformance
signals.text: The G10 scorecard records JPY as the week's leader at an average +1.454% across 7 pairs, while NZD lags the complex at -0.757% across 4 pairs, creating a 2.211% bilateral spread. JPY strength unfolds despite negative carry where overnight OCR sits at 2.7500% against TONA at 0.9770%, alongside a 5-year high in Japan's Reuters Tankan factory sentiment. COT shows NZD leveraged funds net short -23,004 contracts at the 4th percentile of its 52-week range, while JPY speculative positioning sits heavily short at -111,297 contracts at the 2nd percentile. Cross-market pricing reflects structural unwinding, with the pair trading at a -3.94 standard deviation deficit against its BEER fair value model. Technicals on NZD/USD confirm baseline softness below its SMA20 at 0.5908. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/JPY, downside momentum driven by JPY outperformance overriding carry deficits. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 78% hike priced) on 18 Sep. Risk: Sharp risk-on rebound compressing the 2.211% G10 spread and reviving carry flows into high-yielders.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Downside Options Skew + Positioning Unwind
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 153.45, positioned below its SMA20 at 158.45, SMA50 at 160.16, and SMA200 at 158.43. Saxo 25-delta risk reversals print at -2.46 for 1-month tenors, marking an extreme put skew that indicates acute institutional demand for downside protection. CFTC data reveals JPY leveraged funds net short -111,297 contracts with a 52-week percentile of 2 and z-score of -2.18, following a heavy WoW liquidation of -29,678 contracts. Although Fed SOFR at 3.65% holds a +267bp carry advantage over BoJ TONA at 0.98%, the 1-month implied volatility of 10.6% trades below 30-day realized volatility of 11.3%, leaving a negative vol risk premium of -0.7%. Downside momentum dominates despite positive USD carry as crowded speculative shorts continue to cover. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, positioning squeeze and put skew favoring downside extension below moving-average clusters. Catalyst: US PPI release at 12:30 UTC. Risk: Spot recovery above the SMA200 at 158.43 halting the short-covering cycle.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Speculative Long + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7222, holding above its SMA20 at 0.7151, SMA50 at 0.7054, and SMA200 at 0.6995. CFTC positioning shows institutional leveraged funds crowded long at +50,250 contracts, sitting at the 94th percentile of the 52-week range with a z-score of +1.79, even as net weekly additions stalled by -3,328 contracts. In contrast, Myfxbook retail sentiment registers an extreme 91% short positioning, reflecting an acute retail-versus-institutional divergence. The currency maintains policy support via RBA AONIA at 4.35% versus Fed SOFR at 3.65%, providing a 70bp carry buffer alongside hawkish rhetoric from Deputy Governor Hauser. However, BEER fair value models show spot rich at +1.75 standard deviations, warning that upside momentum faces structural friction from overextended spec exposure. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; crowded institutional positioning caps near-term upside velocity. Catalyst: China August inflation release. Risk: Weekly close below the SMA20 at 0.7151 triggering liquidation across crowded leveraged longs.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Rate Differential + Technical Boundary Ahead of ECB
signals.text: EUR/USD sits at 1.1631, holding marginally above its SMA20 at 1.1619 and SMA50 at 1.1520, but capped directly under its SMA200 at 1.1638. Cross-currency policy spreads remain firmly dollar-supportive, with Fed SOFR at 3.65% maintaining a +146bp advantage over ECB €STR at 2.19%. Market expectations price rate hike probability at the upcoming ECB meeting, yet institutional positioning remains defensive with EUR leveraged funds net short -52,784 contracts at the 31st percentile. Implied volatility at 5.1% against 30-day realized volatility of 4.6% yields a narrow +0.5% vol risk premium, while 25-delta risk reversals sit flat at -0.21. Technical upside remains structurally constrained by the 200-day moving average and underlying carry deficits. Trade bias: Neutral/bearish EUR/USD, constrained by policy carry differentials below the 200-day moving average. Catalyst: ECB Refinancing Rate decision at 12:15 UTC. Risk: Hawkish ECB policy delivery forcing an impulsive technical breakout above the SMA200 at 1.1638.
